kanji.question: 日
kanji.explanation: 日 means 'day' or 'sun'. Read as にち (nichi) or ひ (hi).

kanji.question: 月
kanji.explanation: 月 means 'moon' or 'month'. Read as つき (tsuki) or がつ (gatsu).

kanji.question: 山
kanji.explanation: 山 means 'mountain'. Read as やま (yama) or さん (san).

kanji.question: 川
kanji.explanation: 川 means 'river'. Read as かわ (kawa) or かせん (kasen).

kanji.question: 木
kanji.explanation: 木 means 'tree' or 'wood'. Read as き (ki) or もく (moku).

kanji.question: 火
kanji.explanation: 火 means 'fire'. Read as ひ (hi) or か (ka).

kanji.question: 水
kanji.explanation: 水 means 'water'. Read as みず (mizu) or すい (sui).

kanji.question: 土
kanji.explanation: 土 means 'earth' or 'soil'. Read as つち (tsuchi) or ど (do).

kanji.question: 金
kanji.explanation: 金 means 'gold' or 'money'. Read as かね (kane) or きん (kin).

kanji.question: 人
kanji.explanation: 人 means 'person'. Read as ひと (hito) or じん (jin).

kanji.question: 口
kanji.explanation: 口 means 'mouth'. Read as くち (kuchi) or こう (kou).

kanji.question: 目
kanji.explanation: 目 means 'eye'. Read as め (me) or もく (moku).

kanji.question: 耳
kanji.explanation: 耳 means 'ear'. Read as みみ (mimi) or じ (ji).

kanji.question: 手
kanji.explanation: 手 means 'hand'. Read as て (te) or しゅ (shu).

kanji.question: 足
kanji.explanation: 足 means 'foot' or 'leg'. Read as あし (ashi) or そく (soku).

kanji.question: 大
kanji.explanation: 大 means 'big'. Read as おおきい (ookii) or だい (dai).

kanji.question: 小
kanji.explanation: 小 means 'small'. Read as ちいさい (chiisai) or しょう (shou).

kanji.question: 上
kanji.explanation: 上 means 'above' or 'up'. Read as うえ (ue) or じょう (jou).

kanji.question: 下
kanji.explanation: 下 means 'below' or 'down'. Read as した (shita) or か (ka).

kanji.question: 中
kanji.explanation: 中 means 'middle' or 'inside'. Read as なか (naka) or ちゅう (chuu).

kanji.question: 一
kanji.explanation: 一 means 'one'. Read as いち (ichi) or いつ (itsu).

kanji.question: 二
kanji.explanation: 二 means 'two'. Read as に (ni) or じ (ji).

kanji.question: 三
kanji.explanation: 三 means 'three'. Read as さん (san) or みつ (mitsu).

kanji.question: 四
kanji.explanation: 四 means 'four'. Read as よん (yon) or し (shi).

kanji.question: 五
kanji.explanation: 五 means 'five'. Read as ご (go) or いつ (itsu).

grammar.question: 私___学生です。(I am a student.)
grammar.explanation: は (wa) is the topic marker particle. 私は (watashi wa) = 'As for me / I am'

grammar.question: 本___読みます。(I read a book.)
grammar.explanation: を (wo) marks the direct object. 本を読む = 'read a book'

grammar.question: 学校___行きます。(I go to school.)
grammar.explanation: に (ni) marks direction/destination. 学校に行く = 'go to school'

grammar.question: 図書館___勉強します。(I study at the library.)
grammar.explanation: で (de) marks location of action. 図書館で = 'at the library'

grammar.question: これ___私のかばんです。(This is my bag.)
grammar.explanation: は (wa) is the topic marker. これは = 'This (topic)'

grammar.question: 毎日、朝ごはん___食べます。(I eat breakfast every day.)
grammar.explanation: を marks the direct object. 朝ごはんを食べる = 'eat breakfast'

grammar.question: 友達___手紙を書きます。(I write a letter to a friend.)
grammar.explanation: に marks indirect object/recipient. 友達に書く = 'write to a friend'

grammar.question: 電車___来ます。(I come by train.)
grammar.explanation: で marks means of transport. 電車で = 'by train'

grammar.question: 猫___います。(There is a cat.)
grammar.explanation: が marks the subject with います/あります. 猫が = 'cat (subject)'

grammar.question: 明日___学校に行きません。(I will not go to school tomorrow.)
grammar.explanation: Correct order: 明日は学校に行きません。Time expressions usually come first.

vocabulary.question: What does 'ありがとう' mean?
vocabulary.explanation: ありがとう (arigatou) means 'Thank you'. ありがとうございます is the polite form.

vocabulary.question: What does 'おはようございます' mean?
vocabulary.explanation: おはようございます (ohayou gozaimasu) means 'Good morning'.

vocabulary.question: What does 'すみません' mean?
vocabulary.explanation: すみません (sumimasen) means 'Excuse me' or 'I'm sorry'.

vocabulary.question: What does '見る' mean?
vocabulary.explanation: 見る (miru) means 'to see' or 'to watch'.

vocabulary.question: What does '聞く' mean?
vocabulary.explanation: 聞く (kiku) means 'to listen' or 'to ask'.
